Thanks Duds! Yeah my reason for looking for longs was the fact that all
 the cycles were playing out to set up for a bull run (we were in
monthly demand, got the close above near term resistance in the weekly,
and we got the daily engulf during the last rally) so that's why I was

Thanks IF,

But this brings about a couple more questions regarding PA and
stops. Now when it comes to levels and stops, I was always under the
belief that if a new level was created during active market hours within
 your zone, then that becomes your new trade/ risk area. A little
unwritten rule of thumb that I have myself is that at least a new 1hr,
30 min, or 15 min embedded zone has to be created for me to make that my
 NEW trade/ risk area upon revisit since higher TFs are more reliable.
Here is an example of a trade I took yesterday on the CADCHF.

1hr

4hr

As you can see, the trade I took was a plane jane trade that was simply
based off of the 4hr zone that cause the consumption of upper supply.
Since we were still clearly in an uptrend with a plausible 4hr target
overhead yet to be hit, I figured I would go for it even though we
didn't get the full engulf. The trade worked out fine, but in the LTFs,
 I watched the action develop, and a setup that I have always considered
 valid came up.

Here is the setup I'm talking about as previously mentioned in the first two paragraphs,

1hr

As you can see, there was a new 1hr demand zone that was created WITHIN
my 4hr zone during the active market hours. In my mind, this was a high
 probability trade which I would have probably taken on the retest if I
wasn't already in the trade. My logic for this is if a NEW 1hr demand
zone was created when pro money was active, then why have my stop beyond
 the original 4hr zone? Whey not enter on the retrace to the newly
created 1hr demand and have your stop below that? That is the same
logic I had in my EURGBP trade, so assuming we did get the proper PA and
 engulfed the 1min FO level, why would my stop still need to be below
the original zone you showed since this would have been a NEW 1hr demand
 zone within the 4hr demand??

The way I have always looked at it, playing PA to the right like this
increases RR and I have seen it work a hundred times before in my
studies. As for the TP, it would have stayed the same for me (the
'ultimate profit target' in the 4hr chart) since this was a new 30 min
or greater embedded demand zone. If this were just a newly created 15
min demand zone, I would have switched to 'intraday' mode and my
ultimate TP would have been more conservatively based upon the lower
4hr zone that caused the retrace.

Also, with regard to PA, I personally have a problem with
zooming all the way down to the 1min to check for the limits to be
engulfed because when you get down that low, it seems you can always
make a case (or a least most times) as to whey 'this' or 'that' 1min
zone is the reason price is being held down. It can just get very
messy, confusing, and paralyzing when you go down that low to look for
confirmation because there are rarely places in the chart where one will
 have a complete liquidity gap/ pole down to the 1 min. If I were to
scrutinize every trade I took to this level, well, I don't think I would
 ever take a trade because this is a perfect setup and the market rarely
 provides those in my eyes, which is why we have stops in the first
place.

Sorry for these long drawn out questions, but I feel these are key
issues I have been battling with for a while now without avail.

Long ago I gave up on the idea that the orders have literally been lying there since the move was made.

In the short term, sure it may be the case, but in the very long term, I think probably not.

That point is moot, however, as the orders tend to get put there before price arrives again.

When the ITs make trade plans, they look for levels to work from and to.
 They don't just target the middle of space to take profits and turn;
they look for a place with history.

Any IT worth his salt will always know where the main mover is taking price to.

It's simply a club. Don't forget that!
